1:
- **Step 7, Clinical Director "meeting QP standards".** QP alone is not enough for SAIOP or SACOT leadership. The rules require an LCAS or CCS on site at least 50 percent of hours for SAIOP (10A NCAC 27G .4402) and 90 percent for SACOT (.4502). CCP 8A-12 and 8A-13 (amended Jan 1, 2026) also allow a Clinical Supervisor Intern. QP applies to direct care staff and the CCP 8G program supervisor ([27G rules](http://reports.oah.state.nc.us/ncac/title%2010a%20-%20health%20and%20human%20services/chapter%2027%20-%20mental%20health,%20community%20facilities%20and%20services/subchapter%20g/subchapter%20g%20rules.html), [CCP 8A-12](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/15767/download), [CCP 8A-13](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/15769/download)).
- **QP item number.** The QP definition is now item (21) of 10A NCAC 27G .0104 after the Jan 1, 2024 amendment. The .4402 and .4502 text still cites item (18).
- **"Facility Director (named on license)".** The DHSR application names the Facility Director on the form, but the license is issued to the licensee entity. I found no source making the director the "legal responsible party" ([DHSR application](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/pdf/mhiapp.pdf)).
- **Step 5, insurance "required by DHSR".** The DHSR application packet does not mention insurance. The $1M/$3M limits come from LME/MCO terms, for example [Alliance](https://www.alliancehealthplan.org/providers/network/qa/insurance/), and the DHHS model contract leaves limits to each LME/PIHP.
- **Step 5, "name the agency as primary insured".** Your agency is the named insured. The plan is the certificate holder, or additional insured where required. Primary and non-contributory is an endorsement, not a role.
- **Step 6, "voided check for NCTracks EFT".** NCTracks takes EFT data keyed into the enrollment application or portal, and the sources I read do not require a check or bank letter ([NCTracks job aid](https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/dam/jcr:b77caef7-8592-4d5a-9c65-9798ca6a13f2/JA_PRV531_Add-Updt%20EFT%20Info_W2.0.1.pdf)). The voided check or bank letter is used by LME/MCOs such as Alliance and Trillium.
- **Step 4, $50-$200 zoning fee and 3-6 weeks.** Neither is verified statewide. Durham charges $58 and $28 for its two letter types ([Durham](https://www.durhamnc.gov/4856/Verification-Letters)).
- **Step 4, main resource.** The NCACC link covers counties only, and city zoning is often municipal. I could not open that page, so it is not verified.
- **Step 4, SAIOP and SACOT building class.** DHSR lists Group B Business Occupancy for adult SAIOP and SACOT. Adolescent day programs cannot be in a Business Occupancy.
- **Step 4, CCP 8G.** Peer Support is not on DHSR's licensed-program list, so DHSR zoning and inspection paperwork may not apply to a peer-support-only site.
- **Step 4, accessibility code.** The OSFM page shows the 2018 NC Building Code as currently effective. The 2024 code's effective date is not settled.
- **Steps 5, 6 and 7, main-resource links.** The NCDOI, FDIC and oah.nc.gov links are generic and do not state the requirements.
- **LME/MCO changes.** Vaya and Partners began combined claims processing as Vaya Partners on Oct 1, 2026, and Trillium's unified claims platform took effect the same day ([Vaya Partners](https://providers.vayahealth.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/8_24_26_ProviderMergerInfoSession.pdf), [Trillium](https://www.trilliumhealthresources.org/sites/default/files/docs/Provider-documents/Claims/Trillium-Unified-Claims-Platform-Presentation-082726.pdf)).
- **CCP versions.** CCP 8A-12 and 8A-13 were amended Jan 1, 2026 and require national accreditation within one year of enrollment. CCP 8G was amended Sept 1, 2026.
2:
- **Letter of Support scope.** The app says it is a mandatory DHSR attachment for all three services. Rule [10A NCAC 27G .0406](http://reports.oah.state.nc.us/ncac/title%2010a%20-%20health%20and%20human%20services/chapter%2027%20-%20mental%20health,%20community%20facilities%20and%20services/subchapter%20g/subchapter%20g%20rules.html) is titled "Letter of Support Required for Licensure of Residential Facilities." The [DHSR packet](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/pdf/mhiapp.pdf) lists the letter only in its 24-hour residential section. The [DHSR establish page](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/establish.html) tells day programs only to contact the LME/MCO for need and contracting.
- **Number of LME/MCOs.** The app lists four plans. Vaya Health and Partners merged on October 1, 2026 as Vaya Partners, leaving Alliance, Trillium and Vaya Partners ([NC DHHS directory](https://www.ncdhhs.gov/providers/lme-mco-directory)). Partners also paused new contracting requests and licensure letters of support effective August 1, 2026.[providers.partnersbhm.org](https://providers.partnersbhm.org/partners-pauses-new-contracting-requests/?share_frome=aipt)
- **Peer Support network status (new).** Peer Support became a mandatory closed-network service for all prepaid health plans on July 7, 2026 under Session Law 2026-41, per NC Medicaid. Alliance says July 2, 2026; NC Medicaid is the more authoritative source.[alliancehealthplan.org](https://www.alliancehealthplan.org/providers/network/become-a-provider/provider-enrollment/?share_frome=aipt)[medicaid.ncdhhs.gov](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/providers/provider-playbook-medicaid-managed-care/fact-sheets/mandatory-closed-networks?share_frome=aipt)
- **Peer Support ratio.** The app says a 1:6 QP-to-CPSS ratio. [CCP 8G](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8g-peer-support-services/open), amended September 1, 2026, says QP-to-CPSS is 1:8, CPSS-to-beneficiary is 1:15 (correct in the app), and the group ratio is 1:12. The program must be under a full-time QP.
- **CCP 8G amendment items the app omits.** The September 1, 2026 amendment requires the program to be integrated with CCA, psychotherapy and medication management, or a signed MOU or MOA. It also bars Peer Support at the same time of day as SAIOP or SACOT.
- **SACOT staffing wording.** The app says "Qualified Professionals for group therapy." [CCP 8A-13](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/15769/download) (amended January 1, 2026) uses Licensed Clinical Staff and Certified Clinical Staff, at one per 10 or fewer beneficiaries during group counseling. Rule .4502(b) still uses Qualified Professional at 1:10, so satisfy both.
- **Clinical Supervisor on-site percentages.** The app omits them. Rule .4402 requires 50% of SAIOP hours and .4502 requires 90% of SACOT hours. The CCPs also allow a Clinical Supervisor Intern and a split of the role between two staff.
- **"Ten-element" service note and "APSM 45-2".** The [July 2025 DHHS manual](https://www.ncdhhs.gov/rmdmjuly-2025/download?attachment) (effective July 8, 2025) lists ten content bullets, then authentication, then CCP-specific additions. CCP 8G lists eleven elements (a through k). The manual text no longer prints the label "APSM 45-2".
- **Policy "review tool".** The DHSR document is the [Policy and Procedure Workbook](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/pdf/PolicyProcedure-Workbook.pdf) (rev 3-20-25). The packet says not to submit policies with the application.
- **IRIS timelines.** "72-hour" is right for Level II (except deaths) and Level III reports, but the app omits the 24-hour internal review team and the 24-hour HCPR report. IRIS stands for Incident Response Improvement System, not "critical incident" ([rule .0603 and .0604](http://reports.oah.state.nc.us/ncac/title%2010a%20-%20health%20and%20human%20services/chapter%2027%20-%20mental%20health,%20community%20facilities%20and%20services/subchapter%20g/subchapter%20g%20rules.html); [Trillium bulletin](https://www.trilliumhealthresources.org/sites/default/files/docs/Network-Communication-Bulletin/466-Network-Communication-Bulletin.pdf)).
- **42 CFR Part 2 "modernized".** The revised rule required compliance by February 16, 2026, so it is already mandatory ([HHS fact sheet](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/regulatory-initiatives/fact-sheet-42-cfr-part-2-final-rule/index.html), [eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-2)).
- **Timing.** The "2–6 weeks" estimate for a letter is unverified. Under .0406(e) the LME must respond to a residential request within five business days, and Alliance also states five business days for provider applications.
- **Resource link.** pss.unc.edu is the NC CPSS program only. LCAS and CCS credentials are verified through NCASPPB.[pss.unc.edu](https://pss.unc.edu/?share_frome=aipt)[ncsappb.org](https://www.ncsappb.org/credentialing/licensed-clinical-addiction-specialist/?share_frome=aipt)
3:
- Licensing fee: the App context says "$350 base fee + $12.50/day client capacity fee". Non-residential facilities pay a flat $265.00 with no capacity fee, per the [DHSR FAQ](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/faq.html) and the [application packet](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/pdf/mhiapp.pdf). The $350 is the residential fee for 6 beds or fewer.
- LME/MCO Letter of Support: the App context lists it as an application attachment. It is required for 24-hour residential programs only, per [10A NCAC 27G .0406 and the packet](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/pdf/mhiapp.pdf). It does not appear on the Day Program Checklist.
- Policies and staff roster: the packet says policies are not sent with the application, and the checklist has no roster. The [FAQ](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/faq.html) says the manual goes to the consultant at first review.
- CCP 8G licensure: DHSR does not license Peer Support Services, per the [new provider presentation](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/pdf/newprovider.pdf). Step 14 applies to SAIOP and SACOT only. Steps 13 and 11 apply to a peer-support-only site only as good practice, and that is NOT VERIFIED.
- "SAMHSA exclusion logs": no SAMHSA exclusion list was found. Use OIG LEIE, SAM.gov and the [NC Medicaid exclusion list](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/providers/excluded-providers).[oig.hhs.gov](https://oig.hhs.gov/exclusions/background.asp?share_frome=aipt)[sam.gov](https://sam.gov/content/exclusions?share_frome=aipt)
- HCPR scope: the statute defines health care personnel as unlicensed staff, but 10A NCAC 27G .0202(b)(4) applies to all service providers. The App context's "Sex Offender Registry" check is not required by any source found.
- SBI cost "$35 - $75": the [SBI access agreement form](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/abcms/pdf/Non-Criminal-Justice-Access-Agreement-Form_SB-41.pdf) lists $38 per fingerprint card for the national check. The State-only fee is NOT VERIFIED.
- CPSS training: Foundations is 60 hours on Track A, and 50 hours is the Track B approved course, per the [program certification page](https://pss.unc.edu/certification). The 20 hours are prerequisite training, not continuing education. The 18 months of recovery is correct. Recertification is every two years and needs 20 hours.
- CPSS program affiliation: "UNC School of Social Work" was not stated on the pages opened. The program site is pss.unc.edu.
- Fire and sanitation: "$75-$250" fees are NOT VERIFIED. The OAH fire code document shows a three-year state minimum for business occupancies, but 10A NCAC 27G .0402(d)(3) requires annual compliance. Sanitation is required for day programs only if you serve food.[oah.nc.gov](https://www.oah.nc.gov/bcc-fire-code-final-revised-rule/open?share_frome=aipt)
4:
- **Step 15, "4-8 weeks queue wait":** NOT VERIFIED. DHSR states only that an applicant has six months from first contact with a Licensure and Training team member to meet all requirements ([DHSR application packet](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/pdf/mhiapp.pdf)).
- **Step 15, "$0 (included in filing)":** Mostly right. The $265 non-residential initial license fee is paid with the application, and G.S. 122C-23 bars issuance until it is paid ([DHSR packet](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/pdf/mhiapp.pdf)).
- **Step 15, applies to CCP 8G:** The matrix lists no DHSR license for Peer Support, but does for SAIOP and SACOT ([Provider Permission Matrix](https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/dam/jcr:4f0d2400-62b7-48a3-9617-ad31dd8cf543/Provider%20Permission%20Matrix%2008-16-2026.xlsx)). Steps 15 and 16 may not apply to an 8G-only site.
- **Step 15, 10A NCAC 27G .0209:** This rule is Medication Requirements. Restrictive interventions are in 10A NCAC 27E .0101 to .0108 ([OAH 27E .0104](http://reports.oah.state.nc.us/ncac/title%2010a%20-%20health%20and%20human%20services/chapter%2027%20-%20mental%20health,%20community%20facilities%20and%20services/subchapter%20e/10a%20ncac%2027e%20.0104.pdf)).[reports.oah.state.nc.us](http://reports.oah.state.nc.us/ncac/title%2010a%20-%20health%20and%20human%20services/chapter%2027%20-%20mental%20health,%20community%20facilities%20and%20services/subchapter%20g/10a%20ncac%2027g%20.0209.pdf?share_frome=aipt)
- **Step 16, "10-15 calendar days":** DHSR's template says return the POC within 10 days of receipt of the SOD. No 15-day figure was found ([Provider Resource Manual](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/pdf/train/resource.pdf), rev. 9/4/2019).
- **Step 16, correction timing:** Correction deadlines run from the survey exit date: A1/A2 23 days, B 45 days, standard 60 days, re-cited standard 30 days ([Provider Resource Manual](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/pdf/train/resource.pdf)).
- **Step 16, "2-4 weeks" to license:** DHSR says issuing a license or MHL number may take up to three weeks ([Walk-Through form](https://info.ncdhhs.gov/dhsr/mhlcs/pdf/FacilityWalk-Through.pdf)).
- **Step 17, "mandatory full participation agreement ... online":** The agreement is a PDF emailed to hiea@nc.gov or mailed, not signed online. Several types exist, and a Submission-only option is available.[hiea.nc.gov](https://hiea.nc.gov/providers/how-connect/nc-healthconnex-participation-agreement?share_frome=aipt)
- **Step 17, "3-6 weeks":** HIEA says to allow 6 to 8 weeks to receive the executed agreement.[hiea.nc.gov](https://hiea.nc.gov/providers/how-connect/nc-healthconnex-participation-agreement?share_frome=aipt)
- **Step 17, dependency on Step 16 (license):** No source requires the DHSR license before signing. HIEA's page asks only for entity and contact details.
- **Step 17, "HL7/FHIR" and "certified EHR":** HIEA asks only that the EHR can send HL7 version 2.0 or higher. ONC certification is preferred, not required. FHIR is for health plan data access.[hiea.nc.gov](https://hiea.nc.gov/providers/how-connect/nc-healthconnex-participation-agreement?share_frome=aipt)
- **Step 17, "approved HIEA extension":** The hardship extension in G.S. 90-414.4(a3) cannot extend beyond the statutory deadline of January 1, 2023 ([NC HIEA](https://hiea.nc.gov/providers/what-does-law-mandate)).
- **Step 17, "proof of connection before billing":** No source found requires this. See Open Questions.
- **Step 17, Part 2 records:** Records subject to 42 CFR Part 2 are exempt from submission under G.S. 90-414.4(c) ([NC HIEA](https://hiea.nc.gov/providers/what-does-law-mandate)). SAIOP and SACOT may hold such records.
- **Step 18, "$709 federal application fee":** The 2026 federal fee is $750. The $100 NC fee is correct.[nctracks.nc.gov](https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/public/providers/faq-main-page/faqs-for-Behavioral-Health-Provider-Enrollment.html?share_frome=aipt)[medicaid.ncdhhs.gov](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/provider-enrollment-2026-summer-and-fall-series-1-powerpoint/open?share_frome=aipt)
- **Step 18, "assign taxonomy codes" (plural):** The matrix lists one taxonomy, 251S00000X, with each service selected under it ([Provider Permission Matrix](https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/dam/jcr:4f0d2400-62b7-48a3-9617-ad31dd8cf543/Provider%20Permission%20Matrix%2008-16-2026.xlsx)).
- **Step 18, "attach DHSR license":** The Sept 2025 guide lists no license upload. NCTracks verifies it, and the matrix flags it as source-verified.[nctracks.nc.gov](https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/dam/jcr:8d0d2b03-b987-41b2-855c-cb5d1ad4980f/PUGPRV593.pdf?share_frome=aipt)
- **Step 18, W-9 and banking documents:** The W-9 is an electronic attestation. EFT details are entered on an EFT Account Information page ([HSO guide](https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/dam/jcr:7d4728a7-9427-4ebb-9d21-3f1262cbf772/PUG_Human%20Service%20Organization%20Enrollment%20Participant%20User%20Guide.pdf)). No bank document upload was found.[per.nctracks.com](https://per.nctracks.com/content/public/providers/provider-enrollment/terms-and-conditions.html?share_frome=aipt)
- **Step 18, dependency on Step 17 (HIE):** The Sept 2025 Organization guide has no HIE step.
- **Step 18, additional requirements not in app context:**
  - The Office Administrator must be an owner or managing employee.[nctracks.nc.gov](https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/dam/jcr:8d0d2b03-b987-41b2-855c-cb5d1ad4980f/PUGPRV593.pdf?share_frome=aipt)
  - The matrix shows taxonomy 251S00000X as high risk with a site visit and fingerprinting.
  - New Provider Training is due within 15 calendar days.
  - Taxonomy 251S00000X needs a service selected, with an extended deadline of October 1, 2026.[medicaid.ncdhhs.gov](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/provider-enrollment-2026-summer-and-fall-series-1-powerpoint/open?share_frome=aipt)
5:
- **Managing employees and fingerprinting (Step 19).** The app says 5%+ owners and managing employees must be fingerprinted. NCTracks says fingerprint checks apply to high-risk providers and owners with 5% or greater direct or indirect ownership, and states managing employees are not required to be fingerprinted ([NCTracks fingerprinting FAQ](https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/public/providers/faq-main-page/faqs-for-fingerprinting.html)). The statute still lets NC Medicaid raise risk based on a managing employee's history ([G.S. 108C-3](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_108C/GS_108C-3.html)).
- **$38 fingerprint cost.** NOT VERIFIED. The FAQ says the person notified pays, and the cost varies by location.
- **"Fingerprint Verification Forms" to a "Provider Screening Unit."** The actual document is the NCTracks-generated Electronic Fingerprint Submission Release of Information form. It is uploaded to the application under Upload Documents; mailed forms are not processed.
- **"30-day notice window."** Not stated in the current FAQ. The deadline is the one in your notice.
- **Step 19 scope.** The app lists only 8A-12 and 8A-13. The Aug. 16, 2026 Provider Permission Matrix shows Peer Support Services (8G), SAIOP and SACOT all as High risk under taxonomy 251S00000X, with site visit, application fee and fingerprinting required ([Provider Permission Matrix](https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/dam/jcr:4f0d2400-62b7-48a3-9617-ad31dd8cf543/Provider%20Permission%20Matrix%2008-16-2026.xlsx)). So Step 19 also applies to 8G.
- **Missing fees.** High-risk enrollment carries a 2026 federal application fee of $750 plus the $100 NC fee ([NCTracks fee table](https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/dam/jcr:5088259c-ab17-4c01-bf6d-c64786be1da4/State%20and%20Federal%20Fee%20Amounts%20by%20Year.xlsx)). The app's $0 cost for Step 20 and $38 for Step 19 do not reflect these.
- **Step 20 affiliations.** The Manage Change Request must be initiated by the Office Administrator of the individual provider's record, not by the organization ([Medicaid Bulletin June 2017](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/documents/files/medicaid-bulletin-2017-06/open)). CCS and QP are not NCTracks provider types; LCAS may be, if enrolled individually.
- **Step 21 plan list.** The app names Alliance, Partners, Trillium and Vaya. Vaya Health and Partners combined as Vaya Partners on Oct. 1, 2026 ([Vaya Partners enrollment page](https://providers.vayapartners.org/enrollment/); joint merger session).[providers.vayahealth.com](https://providers.vayahealth.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Joint_VP_Merger_Info_Session_9-14-26.pdf?share_frome=aipt)
- **Step 21 main resource.** There is no single "Regional LME/MCO Contracting Portal." Each plan has its own enrollment page and process.
- **Peer Support network access.** Under Session Law 2026-41, NC Medicaid says plans must maintain closed networks for Peer Support Services and may exclude providers, effective July 7, 2026 ([NC Medicaid fact sheet](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/providers/provider-playbook-medicaid-managed-care/fact-sheets/mandatory-closed-networks)). G.S. 108D-23(b) was repealed by Session Law 2026-1 ([G.S. 108D-23](https://www.ncleg.gov/EnactedLegislation/Statutes/HTML/BySection/Chapter_108D/GS_108D-23.html)). Alliance cites Senate Bill 257 effective July 2, 2026, which differs from NC Medicaid's July 7 date; NC Medicaid is the more authoritative source.
- **CAQH IDs.** None of the plan pages opened ask for CAQH, and NC Medicaid says LME/MCOs no longer perform credentialing ([NCTracks BH enrollment FAQ](https://www.nctracks.nc.gov/content/public/providers/faq-main-page/faqs-for-Behavioral-Health-Provider-Enrollment.html)). Treat CAQH as NOT VERIFIED and unrequired until a plan requests it.
- **APSM 45-2 and "10 elements" (Step 22).** The current rulebook is the NC DHHS Record Management and Documentation Manual, effective July 8, 2025 ([RM&DM](https://www.ncdhhs.gov/rmdmjuly-2025/download?attachment)). It lists about ten content elements plus electronic authentication and CCP-specific additions, and I found no mention of APSM 45-2 in the text reviewed. CCP 8G also adds start and end times.
- **SACOT code.** The app says H2036. CCP 8A-13 lists H2035, one unit equal to one hour, with a 4-hour daily minimum to bill ([CCP 8A-13](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/15769/download?attachment)).
- **SAIOP billing.** H0015 is one unit per day as an event, with a 3-hour minimum ([CCP 8A-12](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/media/15767/download?attachment)). The policy's 2-hour adolescent figure is a scheduling minimum, not a billing minimum.
- **"Same-day" exclusion.** Both CCPs bar SAIOP and SACOT in the same episode of care, not just the same day, except on the day of admission or discharge. They also bar billing with individual, family or group SUD therapy in that episode.
- **Peer Support limits.** CCP 8G (amended Sept. 1, 2026) has no 20-unit daily or 80-unit weekly cap. It has 24 unmanaged units per episode, then 176 units per 60 days and no more than 88 per 30 days without additional review. H0038 is a 15-minute unit ([CCP 8G](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/8g-peer-support-services/open)).
- **EHR cost and resource.** The $150 to $400 per clinician per month figure and the healthit.gov link are NOT VERIFIED. Healthit.gov is a federal information site, not a behavioral health EHR vendor directory.
